note: Every figure the deck prints that is not the source's own words repeated. Each names where it came from, and the gate re-derives it. 'Eight slots' and 'Two agencies' were removed when frame 8's hook and dek were rewritten in round 3, rather than left declared for a later run to reuse.

aggregates.quote: Over 1.1 million pedestrians exit the U.S. to Mexico annually, and it is imperative to keep them safely moving,
aggregates.why: The bridge director's own figure for the crossing, repeated rather than computed. It measures the crossing and not the technology, which is the deck's whole angle.

aggregates.quote: In early 2026, S&T invited six companies to the Maryland Test Facility (MdTF) for basic capability demonstrations to determine which solutions should be operationally tested.
aggregates.why: The account's own count of companies demonstrated. Not a tally of claims and not arithmetic.

aggregates.quote: These demonstrations led CBP and S&T to select three solutions for additional data collection: two from NEC National Security Systems (NSS) and one joint solution from Paravision and AiFi.
aggregates.why: The account's own count of solutions carried forward. The slide sets it capitalised at the head of a sentence and the caption sets it lower case mid sentence, and it is one count off one claim either way.

aggregates.computed_by: out/2026-09-04/compute.py, may_inbound_pedestrians. The value is read out of the fetched data row in c26 with a regular expression rather than retyped, and its thousands separator is applied by code. A separator is a formatting decision and this project does not let a writer make one.
aggregates.why: It is a count of people ENTERING the United States at this port in May 2026. It is not a count of the people the cameras watched, who were walking the other way, and both the slide and the caption say entering.

aggregates.computed_by: out/2026-09-04/compute.py, performance_facts_asked and performance_facts_published. Three is the count of verdict claims the frame seats, c7 and c9 and c31, each string a literal substring of its own claim's quote. Five is the count of named absences, each established by its own claim, c18 accuracy, c19 images captured, c20 retention, c21 deployment and c22 assessment dates. Eight is those two counts added, which is the number of cavities the frame cuts. Neither three nor five is a tally over an unnamed set.
aggregates.why: The five named absences compute.py enumerates, one per claim.

aggregates.computed_by: out/2026-09-04/compute.py, characterisations_quoted. It is the length of the frame's own seated list, c7 and c9 and c31, each string a literal substring of its own claim's verified quote and each attributed on the frame to the party that said it. All three are the source's own words: two inside a named speaker's quotation and one the line that closes a third speaker's. It is a count of quotations and never a count of findings, because a characterisation is not a measurement and the frame's whole argument is that distinction.
aggregates.why: Frame 8's hook reads 'Three quotes. No measurement.' The previous hook counted the three and the five in one eight slot form, and a round 3 judge read that as telling a two second reader the account is three eighths answered, on the one frame whose job is to say it answered nothing. The three and the five are different kinds and the hook now says so.
